companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce (核心本地商业) segment operating profit/(loss)
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's disclosed Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/loss. The segment bundles food delivery, Instashopping and in-store/hotel/travel, and it carries most of the subsidy cost. Meituan does not break out a delivery-only loss. Q3 2026 results were not out as of Nov 25-26. Q3 2025 results came on Nov 28, 2025, so expect a similar date.

filing: FY2025 results, 2026-03-26; approximate, from Chinese press, not re-verified
derived: H1 2026 segment profit RMB3.6bn less Q2 RMB5.7bn; segment margin -3.2% per 163.com coverage
filing: Meituan Q2 2026 results, 2026-08-28; margin +7.9% vs +5.7% a year earlier, +52.3% YoY (163.com, Zhihu)

companies.latest_signal: Core Local Commerce swung to a RMB5.7bn operating profit in Q2 2026, after losses of about RMB14bn, RMB10bn and RMB2bn in the prior three quarters. Group operating profit also turned positive at RMB2.7bn, ending three loss-making quarters. Chinese coverage (163.com) credits the regulator halting large-scale universal subsidies in June 2026. Q2 is a high base, and the Q3 print will show whether it holds.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: Taobao Shangou (Flash Sale)/Ele.me instant-retail loss (sell-side estimates; no company-disclosed loss figure)
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not disclose a standalone instant-commerce loss. It reports instant-retail revenue and qualitative commentary ('losses continue to narrow', unit economics improving q/q). The loss values below are analyst estimates (CICC, Guosen, Huayuan) quoted in Chinese financial press, not company disclosures. They are calendar-quarter figures and not fully verified.

Aug 2026 results gave only a q/q unit-economics improvement. No loss figure was disclosed.
Zhitong Finance preview; results on Nov 19-20, 2026 gave no loss figure. Instant-retail revenue was RMB58.76bn, +22% YoY (Ebrun)

companies.latest_signal: In the Nov 2026 results, management said Flash Sale market share is stable, losses continue to narrow and unit economics improve q/q. Ebrun reports a goal of halving losses next year and reaching profitability by FY2029. Group adjusted EBITA rose 260% YoY to RMB32.6bn, and Ebrun credits Flash Sale and cloud improvements. The direction is clear, but the size of the loss is unconfirmed and rests on estimates.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_name: New Businesses (新业务) segment operating loss
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed New Businesses segment operating loss. It includes JD Takeaway (food delivery), Jingxi, JD Property and overseas. JD does not disclose a standalone food-delivery loss. A segment reclassification in Q3 2026 cut segment revenue and may flatter the comparison.

companies.latest_signal: JD says its food-delivery loss narrowed by more than 50% YoY and about 7% q/q, helped by lower per-order subsidies, delivery efficiency and higher commission and ad revenue. Orders and users both grew q/q. The segment loss improved only about RMB0.2bn q/q (9.85 to 9.64), so the pace has slowed sharply. JD gave no breakeven date and only targets a 'significant' further YoY loss reduction in 2027.

war_summary: Losses are narrowing, and the war has cooled sharply from its Q3 2025 peak. Meituan's core segment is back to a RMB5.7bn profit in Q2 2026, Alibaba's estimated Flash Sale loss is down from about RMB37bn to about RMB9bn a quarter, and JD's New Businesses loss is down 39% YoY to RMB9.6bn. Chinese coverage (163.com) credits the June 2026 regulatory halt on large universal subsidies and the broader anti-involution push. Nobody has formally blinked on share: Alibaba says Flash Sale share is stable, and Meituan's Q3 print (still pending) is the key test of whether its profit holds. The improvement is flattening at JD, and Alibaba still carries about RMB9bn a quarter on estimates, so both remain exposed if subsidies re-escalate.
